title: Piet Mondrian's birth chart
metaDescription: Piet Mondrian's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.3° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun and Pluto sit 0.9° from an exact sextile — near enough that the tradition reads identity and depth as a single working part. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Pisces, but precisely: 17.3°, second decan, 10°–20°, under the Moon in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 14.1° Pisces, Venus at 13.9° Aquarius, Mars at 4.2° Aries. Mercury in a water sign reads as a mind that absorbs before it argues; Venus in a air sign reads as taste led by wit and proportion; Mars in a fire sign reads as drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Saturn to Pluto is the closest call of the day, a trine within 0.9°. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it. Behind it, the Sun sextile Pluto at 0.9°, and Jupiter opposition Saturn at 0.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Jupiter opposes Saturn while both square Neptune. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Pisces at 14.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Aries at 4.2° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Cancer at 20.0° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Capricorn at 19.0° is in domicile. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements water 4, air 2, fire 2, earth 2; modalities cardinal 5, fixed 3, mutable 2. Water signs hold memory in the scheme, where nothing is quite finished and little is genuinely forgotten. Jupiter and Uranus were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aquarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.6° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 19.7°.
